seo.metaDescription: Vertical columns of running totals joined by an area, each with a cap for the change and a short note. The last column is highlighted.

props.markdown: A bridge in vertical columns: the start, then a column for the running total after each change. Each column carries a cap for the change that led to it, the new total above and a short note below.

Use `BridgeChart` when the totals matter as much as the changes: a quote that shrinks to the profit you kept, a budget that is spent down in stages. Each column is a running total, so a reader can see what was left after every step. The cap on a column marks the change (loss or gain), `note` names it (“−$260 discount”), and a gradient area joins the totals (`area={false}` removes it). The last column is solid and emphasized; `highlightLast={false}` keeps it as hatched as the rest. A `callout` pins a pill above the last column for the headline numbers, such as “$400 kept | 12.3% margin”.

If you want one row per change that ends in a calculated total, use [WaterfallChart](/docs/waterfall-chart). A bridge shows the totals, a waterfall shows the changes between them.
Every step has a `note`, the short word that follows the change. `highlightLast={false}` keeps the last column hatched like the others, for a result that is not the point of the chart.
`callout` is an array of segments, so it stays serializable: the pill sits above the last column, which is solid by default (`highlightLast`).
What a step leaks (or gains) is drawn as a hatched cap on its column. The `callout` pill is lifted clear of any column labels it reaches over.

`BridgeChart` is built on `Chart`, so it follows the same keyboard model as the other charts: it is a single tab stop, and tabbing in shows the first column with its tooltip and announces it. Arrow keys move to the previous or next column, `Home` and `End` jump to the first and last, `Enter` or `Space` selects the active column when the chart has `onSelect`, and `Esc` clears the active column. `Esc` is only consumed when a column is active, so an enclosing dialog still closes. The widget’s description ends with a keyboard hint (“Use arrow keys to move between points, Home and End for first and last, Escape to clear.”, plus “Press Enter to select.” with `onSelect`); `keyboardHint` replaces it, for example to translate it, and `keyboardHint=""` turns it off.

Screen readers get the chart title and description, then an announcement for each column the keyboard moves to, in the form “2 of 5, After discount, $1,000, −$260 discount”: its position, label, running total and the change with its note. A visually hidden data table with the columns Column, Change and Total follows the chart; `dataTable` renames the caption and headers, or turns it off.

The SVG and the HTML overlay are `aria-hidden`, so a `callout` says nothing to a screen reader. Put the same facts in the `title`, the `description` or the notes, as the job-profit example does with the profit kept. In a very narrow chart `BridgeChart` shows only some column totals and no notes, and a pinned pill can take three lines; the tooltip and the data table still have everything.
The full model is in the [accessibility guide](https://github.com/mwadon/tally-charts/blob/main/docs/a11y.md).
